Domain: Connected Autonomous Vehicle (CAV): an autonomous car that drives its passengers to a destination, as CAV-TEC V2.0 specifies it - what a passenger can ask of it and what it tells, and the terms of the domain.
DescrMetadata: The Domain Type layer of the Domain Knowledge of a CAV, from the web pages of CAV-TEC V2.0 (each item's Source): its Terms and Definitions, its Architecture and the AMS-HCI Message, Route, Route Command IDs and Route Environment IDs Data Types. Only what concerns a human; the words of a passenger are the Synonyms. The places of a CAV (the Domain Instance layer) come from its Offline Map.

Items.Name: take me to
Items.Text: The passenger can ask the CAV to be taken to a destination. The CAV asks its Autonomous Motion Subsystem for the Routes to that destination, possibly through intermediate stops, and proposes them to the passenger, each with the time the CAV is expected to arrive; if the destination cannot be reached, it says so.

Items.Name: select a route
Items.Text: When the CAV has proposed more than one Route, the passenger selects one of them, e.g. the shorter, the faster or the more comfortable.

Items.Name: start
Items.Text: The passenger tells the CAV to start driving the selected Route (Route Command Execute).

Items.Name: wait
Synonyms: let me out for a moment
Items.Text: The passenger asks the CAV to halt for a while and then go on along the same Route (Route Command Suspend): the Route is kept and can be resumed.

Items.Name: go on
Items.Text: The passenger asks the CAV to go on along the Route it had suspended (Route Command Resume).

Items.Name: change the route
Items.Text: The passenger asks the CAV to change the Route, e.g. for another destination or another way (Route Command Change).

Items.Name: stop
Items.Text: The passenger asks the CAV to stop and abandon the Route (Route Command Stop): the trip ends there. To halt and go on later, the passenger asks to wait.

Items.Name: show me
Items.Text: The passenger can ask to see what the CAV perceives outside, or the view from a place the passenger names; the CAV renders it from the Point of View of that place.

Items.Name: proposed routes
Items.Text: The CAV proposes the Routes to the destination, each a sequence of Way Points with the time the CAV is expected at the end of each segment.

Items.Name: driving
Items.Text: Route Status Executing: the CAV is driving the Route it was commanded to drive.

Items.Name: suspended
Items.Text: Route Status Suspended: the CAV has halted and the Route can be resumed.

Items.Name: stopped
Items.Text: Route Status Stopped: the CAV has halted and the Route is abandoned.

Items.Name: arrived
Items.Text: Route Status Arrived: the CAV has stopped at the destination of the Route.

Items.Name: failure
Items.Text: The CAV tells the passenger of a failure of its equipment, e.g. a low battery or a mechanical failure.

Items.Name: ice
Items.Text: A condition of the environment along a Route: ice on the road.

Items.Name: wind
Items.Text: A condition of the environment along a Route: strong wind.

Items.Name: water
Items.Text: A condition of the environment along a Route: water on the road.

Items.Name: pothole
Items.Text: A condition of the environment along a Route: a pothole.

Items.Name: CAV
Items.Text: A Connected Autonomous Vehicle (CAV) is a land-based vehicle that reaches a destination on its own: it interacts with humans and services, senses the environment, exchanges information with other CAVs and CAV-aware entities, and drives itself in compliance with the applicable traffic laws.

Items.Name: Human-CAV Interaction
Items.Text: Human-CAV Interaction (HCI) is the part of the CAV that talks with humans: it recognises a human as a legitimate user, understands the request to be taken to a destination and conducts the dialogue with the Autonomous Motion Subsystem to satisfy it, recognises the identities of several humans and the objects they point at, converses with the passengers, understanding their emotional state, and can present itself as an avatar.

Items.Name: Autonomous Motion Subsystem
Items.Text: The Autonomous Motion Subsystem (AMS) is the central intelligence of the CAV: it plans the Routes, decides how to move and instructs the Motion Actuation Subsystem, using what the Environment Sensing Subsystem perceives and what other CAVs in range tell.

Items.Name: Environment Sensing Subsystem
Items.Text: The Environment Sensing Subsystem (ESS) perceives the environment of the CAV with its sensors - cameras, LiDAR, RADAR, ultrasound, microphones - and the Offline Map, and describes it to the AMS.

Items.Name: Motion Actuation Subsystem
Items.Text: The Motion Actuation Subsystem (MAS) carries out the movements the AMS decides, commanding the Motors (to accelerate), the Brakes (to slow down) and the Wheels (to steer).

Items.Name: during the trip
Items.Text: While the CAV moves, the passenger can converse with it, ask what it perceives, ask about the state of the CAV and of the road, and ask to change, suspend, resume or stop the Route. The AMS may offer alternatives to satisfy the passenger's preferences, e.g. a longer but more comfortable Route or a shorter but bumpier one.

Items.Name: Route
Items.Text: A Route is a sequence of Way Points on an Offline Map, each with the time the CAV is expected to arrive and to leave; it is the plan the CAV follows and records where it actually stopped or slowed down.

Items.Name: Way Point
Items.Text: A Way Point is a point on an Offline Map; a Route is a sequence of them. A destination the passenger names is a Way Point.

Items.Name: Offline Map
Items.Text: An Offline Map is a previously created digital map of an environment, with its metadata: the CAV uses it to know the places and plan the Routes.

Items.Name: Point of View
Items.Text: A Point of View is a Position and an Orientation: where the CAV is and where it faces. A trip goes from the Point of View where the CAV is to the destination Point of View.

Items.Name: Road State
Items.Text: The Road State describes the state of the road the CAV is traversing: weather, water, damage, potholes, roadworks.

Items.Name: CAV State
Items.Text: The CAV State describes the state of the CAV, as the AMS assesses it from what it knows and from what other CAVs and roadside units tell.

Items.Name: Traffic
Items.Text: Traffic is the set of CAVs, other vehicles, humans and objects moving in or near a road.

Items.Name: Traffic Rules
Items.Text: Traffic Rules are the digital representation of the traffic rules applying to an environment: the CAV drives in compliance with them.

Items.Name: Traffic Signals
Items.Text: Traffic Signals are the signals on and around a road - signs, traffic lights - with their positions and meaning.

Items.Name: Weather
Items.Text: Weather data are temperature, humidity, air pressure, ice, wind and water in its various states: the CAV takes them into account.

Items.Name: Remote CAV
Items.Text: A Remote CAV is another CAV in range: the CAV exchanges information with it, and its passengers can exchange messages with the passengers of the Remote CAV through their HCIs.

Items.Name: CAV-aware
Items.Text: A CAV-aware entity has some of the sensing and communication capabilities of a CAV without being one, e.g. a Roadside Unit or a Traffic Light that tells the CAV what it knows.
